blocks.title: Why Retries Need Safety
blocks.body: Networks drop packets and hide responses, so clients frequently retry timed-out calls.

blocks.title: Idempotency
blocks.body: An operation is idempotent when executing the same request once or multiple times leaves the server in the exact same final state, preventing duplicate side effects on retry.

blocks.title: Versioning Responses
blocks.body: An ETag (entity tag) is an opaque identifier assigned by an HTTP server to a specific version of a resource representation.

blocks.title: Updating Orders
blocks.body: Pass the order's ETag in your PUT request so concurrent updates do not overwrite each other. Store the new ETag returned in the response.

planned.name: action-taught-with-steps-and-result
planned.text: Send a conditional PUT request using If-Match

blocks.title: Performing a Conditional PUT
blocks.body: First run GET /orders/42 and copy the ETag header value (for example, "v3"). Next send PUT /orders/42 with the header If-Match: "v3" and the updated JSON body. If no other client modified the order, the server saves the update and returns 200 OK with a new ETag; if the resource changed, the server rejects the write with 412 Precondition Failed.

planned.name: contrast-taught-in-contrast-section
planned.text: Confusing safe HTTP methods with idempotent HTTP methods

blocks.title: Idempotency
blocks.body: Idempotent methods leave server state identical whether invoked once or many times.

blocks.title: Safe vs. Idempotent
blocks.body: Learners often confuse safe methods with idempotent ones. Safe methods such as GET never mutate server state at all, whereas idempotent methods like PUT and DELETE do mutate server state on the first call while ensuring repeated calls produce the same final state.
